draft.text: You came in because you have had sharp, intermittent pain in your right flank that radiates down to your groin for the last two weeks.
We found that your right ureteral stone has not changed in size or location since your prior CT scan.
You have a history of kidney stones and related surgeries, but the exact dates and procedures are unclear.
You will need further evaluation and management for your flank pain, including possible imaging studies and urological evaluation.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you have had pain in your right flank that goes down to your groin for two weeks.
The pain is sharp and happens more when you don't drink enough or after being active.
We did not find any new test results or physical signs during this visit.
You have a history of kidney stones and past surgeries related to them.
Your current pain may be from a kidney stone in your right ureter, as seen in a past CT scan.
You will need more tests and a urology check-up.
You should also share more details about your past surgeries and the exact dates and types of procedures you had.
